competition: Polish Matura, Mathematics, extended level (poziom rozszerzony)

problems.problem:
The figure shows the set of all real numbers satisfying the inequality $|2x-8|\le 10$.
It follows that
(A) $k=2$
(B) $k=4$
(C) $k=5$
(D) $k=9$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2015_p1_fig.png

The function $f$ is defined by the formula
$$f(x)=\begin{cases} x-2 & \text{for } x\le 0,\\ \big||x+3|-4\big| & \text{for } x>0.\end{cases}$$
The equation $f(x)=1$ has exactly
(A) one solution.
(B) two solutions.
(C) four solutions.
(D) five solutions.

The number $\left(3-2\sqrt{3}\right)^3$ is equal to
(A) $27-24\sqrt{3}$
(B) $27-30\sqrt{3}$
(C) $135-78\sqrt{3}$
(D) $135-30\sqrt{3}$

The equation $2\sin x+3\cos x=6$ in the interval $(0,2\pi)$
(A) has no real solutions.
(B) has exactly one real solution.
(C) has exactly two real solutions.
(D) has more than two real solutions.

The distance from the origin of the coordinate system to the line with equation $y=2x+4$ is equal to
(A) $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}$
(B) $\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}$
(C) $\frac{4}{5}$
(D) $4$
Compute the limit $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{11n^3+6n+5}{6n^3+1}-\frac{2n^2+2n+1}{5n^2-4}\right).$$
The numbers $(-1)$ and $3$ are the zeros of a quadratic function $f$. Compute $\frac{f(6)}{f(12)}$.
Prove that for every real number $x$ the inequality $$x^4-x^2-2x+3>0$$ holds.

The angle bisectors of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ inscribed in a circle intersect at four distinct points $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ (see the figure).
Prove that a circle can be circumscribed about the quadrilateral $PQRS$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2015_p9_fig.png

The side lengths of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ are $|AB|=2$, $|BC|=3$, $|CD|=4$, $|DA|=5$. A circle is circumscribed about the quadrilateral $ABCD$. Compute the length of the diagonal $AC$ of this quadrilateral.

The first urn contains 3 white balls and 5 black balls, and the second urn contains 7 white balls and 2 black balls. We draw one ball from the first urn, move it to the second urn, and in addition put into the second urn two more balls of the same colour as the drawn ball. Then we draw two balls from the second urn. Compute the probability of the event that both balls drawn from the second urn are white.

The function $f$ is defined by the formula $f(x)=x^3-2x^2+1$ for every real number $x$. Find the equations of those tangent lines to the graph of $f$ that are parallel to the line with equation $y=4x$.

The quadratic trinomial $f(x)=(m+1)x^2+2(m-2)x-m+4$ is given. Find all values of the parameter $m$ for which the trinomial $f$ has two distinct real roots $x_1$, $x_2$ satisfying the condition $x_1^2-x_2^2=x_1^4-x_2^4$.

The base of the pyramid $ABCDS$ is the square $ABCD$. The lateral edge $SD$ is the height of the pyramid, and its length is twice the length of a base edge. Compute the sine of the angle between the lateral faces $ABS$ and $CBS$ of this pyramid.

The sum of all four coefficients of the polynomial $W(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c$ is equal to $0$. The three roots of this polynomial form an arithmetic sequence with common difference $3$. Compute the coefficients $a$, $b$ and $c$. Consider all possible cases.
We consider all cones whose axial cross-section is a triangle with perimeter $20$. Compute the height and the base radius of the cone with the largest volume. Compute the volume of this cone.

In the expansion of the expression $\left(2\sqrt{3}\,x+4y\right)^3$ the coefficient of the product $xy^2$ is equal to
(A) $32\sqrt{3}$
(B) $48$
(C) $96\sqrt{3}$
(D) $144$

The polynomial $W(x)=6x^3+3x^2-5x+p$ is divisible by the binomial $x-1$ for $p$ equal to
(A) $4$
(B) $-2$
(C) $2$
(D) $-4$

The figure shows part of the graph of a linear fractional (homographic) function $y=f(x)$ whose domain is the set $D=(-\infty,3)\cup(3,+\infty)$.
The equation $|f(x)|=p$ with unknown $x$ has exactly one solution
(A) in two cases: $p=0$ or $p=3$.
(B) in two cases: $p=0$ or $p=2$.
(C) only when $p=3$.
(D) only when $p=2$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2016_p3_fig.png

The function $f(x)=\frac{3x-1}{x^2+4}$ is defined for every real number $x$. The derivative of this function is given by the formula
(A) $f'(x)=\frac{-3x^2+2x+12}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2}$
(B) $f'(x)=\frac{-9x^2+2x-12}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2}$
(C) $f'(x)=\frac{3x^2-2x-12}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2}$
(D) $f'(x)=\frac{9x^2-2x+12}{\left(x^2+4\right)^2}$

The limit satisfies $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\left(pn^2+4n\right)^3}{5n^6-4}=-\frac{8}{5}.$$ It follows that
(A) $p=-8$
(B) $p=4$
(C) $p=2$
(D) $p=-2$

A survey on building a public kindergarten was carried out among 10 thousand residents of a certain town. The results of the survey are shown in the table.
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|}\hline \text{Group} & \text{Number of people supporting the construction} & \text{Number of people not supporting the construction}\\ \hline \text{Women} & 5140 & 1860\\ \hline \text{Men} & 2260 & 740\\ \hline\end{array}$$
Compute the probability of the event that a person chosen at random from among those surveyed supports the construction of the kindergarten, given that this person is a man.

The geometric sequence $(a_n)$ is defined by the formula $a_n=\left(\frac{1}{2x-371}\right)^n$ for $n\ge 1$. All terms of this sequence are positive. Find the smallest integer $x$ for which the infinite series $a_1+a_2+a_3+\ldots$ is convergent.
Prove that for any positive real numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x^2+y^2=2$, the inequality $x+y\le 2$ holds.

A rectangle $ABCD$ is given. The circle inscribed in the triangle $BCD$ is tangent to the diagonal $BD$ at the point $N$. The circle inscribed in the triangle $ABD$ is tangent to the side $AD$ at the point $M$, and the centre $S$ of this circle lies on the segment $MN$, as in the figure.
Prove that $|MN|=|AD|$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2016_p9_fig.png

Find all values of the parameter $a$ for which the graphs of the functions $f$ and $g$, defined by the formulas $f(x)=x-2$ and $g(x)=5-ax$, intersect at a point both of whose coordinates are positive.
Solve the inequality $\frac{2\cos x-\sqrt{3}}{\cos^2 x}<0$ in the interval $[0,2\pi]$.

The quadratic trinomial $f(x)=x^2+2(m+1)x+6m+1$ is given. Find all real values of the parameter $m$ for which this trinomial has two distinct roots $x_1$, $x_2$ of the same sign satisfying the condition $|x_1-x_2|<3$.

The points $A=(30,32)$ and $B=(0,8)$ are adjacent vertices of a quadrilateral $ABCD$ inscribed in a circle. The line with equation $x-y+2=0$ is the only axis of symmetry of this quadrilateral and contains the diagonal $AC$. Compute the coordinates of the vertices $C$ and $D$ of this quadrilateral.

We consider all ten-digit natural numbers in whose decimal representation only the digits $1$, $2$, $3$ may occur, where the digit $1$ occurs exactly three times. Justify that there are $15\,360$ such numbers.

In a regular quadrilateral pyramid $ABCDS$ with base $ABCD$ the height is equal to $5$, and the angle between adjacent lateral faces of the pyramid measures $120^\circ$. Compute the volume of this pyramid.

The parabola with equation $y=2-\frac{1}{2}x^2$ intersects the $Ox$ axis of the coordinate system at the points $A=(-2,0)$ and $B=(2,0)$. We consider all isosceles trapezoids $ABCD$ whose longer base is the segment $AB$ and the endpoints $C$ and $D$ of whose shorter base lie on the parabola (see the figure).
Express the area of the trapezoid $ABCD$ as a function of the first coordinate of the vertex $C$. Compute the coordinates of the vertex $C$ of that one among the considered trapezoids whose area is the largest.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2016_p16_fig.png

The number $\left(\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}-\sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}}\right)^2$ is equal to
(A) $2$
(B) $4$
(C) $\sqrt{3}$
(D) $2\sqrt{3}$

An infinite sequence of numbers is defined by the formula $a_n=\frac{\left(n^2-10n\right)(2-3n)}{2n^3+n^2+3}$ for $n\ge 1$. Then
(A) $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=\frac{1}{2}$
(B) $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=0$
(C) $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=-\infty$
(D) $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=-\frac{3}{2}$

The segment $CD$ is an altitude of the triangle $ABC$ in which $|AD|=|CD|=\frac{1}{2}|BC|$ (see the figure). The circle with centre $C$ and radius $CD$ is tangent to the line $AB$. This circle intersects the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of the triangle at the points $K$ and $L$, respectively.
The inscribed angle $\alpha$ marked in the figure is equal to
(A) $37.5^\circ$
(B) $45^\circ$
(C) $52.5^\circ$
(D) $60^\circ$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2017_p3_fig.png

The point $B=(-4,7)$ and the vector $\vec{u}=[-3,5]$ are given. The point $A$ such that $\overrightarrow{AB}=-3\vec{u}$ has coordinates
(A) $A=(5,-8)$
(B) $A=(-13,22)$
(C) $A=(9,-15)$
(D) $A=(12,24)$
The remainder of the division of the polynomial $W(x)=x^3-2x^2+ax+\frac{3}{4}$ by the binomial $x-2$ is equal to $1$. Compute the value of the coefficient $a$.
The function $f$ is defined by the formula $f(x)=\frac{x-1}{x^2+1}$ for every real number $x$. Find the equation of the tangent line to the graph of this function at the point $P=(1,0)$.
Prove that for any distinct real numbers $x$, $y$ the inequality $$x^2y^2+2x^2+2y^2-8xy+4>0$$ holds.

In the acute triangle $ABC$ the side $AB$ has length $c$, the length of the side $BC$ is equal to $a$, and $\angle ABC=\beta$. The bisector of the angle $ABC$ intersects the side $AC$ of the triangle at the point $E$.
Prove that the length of the segment $BE$ is equal to $\frac{2ac\cdot\cos\frac{\beta}{2}}{a+c}$.

A ball is placed inside a tetrahedron all of whose edges have the same length $6$ in such a way that it has exactly one common point with each face of the tetrahedron. A plane $\pi$ parallel to the base of this tetrahedron divides it into two solids: a pyramid whose volume equals $\frac{8}{27}$ of the volume of the divided tetrahedron, and a frustum. Compute the distance from the centre $S$ of the ball to the plane $\pi$, i.e. the length of the shortest of the segments $SP$, where $P$ is a point of the plane $\pi$.
Solve the equation $\cos 2x+3\cos x=-2$ in the interval $[0,2\pi]$.

A box contains 8 balls labelled with the consecutive natural numbers from $1$ to $8$. We draw one ball, write down the number on it, and then return the ball to the box. We perform this procedure two more times, and thus obtain three written numbers. Compute the probability of drawing balls such that the product of the three written numbers is divisible by $4$. Give the result as a common fraction.

Find all values of the parameter $m$ for which the equation $$4x^2-6mx+(2m+3)(m-3)=0$$ has two distinct real solutions $x_1$ and $x_2$, with $x_1<x_2$, satisfying the condition $$(4x_1-4x_2-1)(4x_1-4x_2+1)<0.$$
Find the equation of the circle passing through the points $A=(-5,3)$ and $B=(0,6)$ whose centre lies on the line with equation $x-3y+1=0$.

The numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ are, respectively, the first, second and third terms of an arithmetic sequence. The sum of these numbers is equal to $27$. The sequence $(a-2,\ b,\ 2c+1)$ is geometric.
Find the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$.
We consider all cylinders with a given total surface area $P$. Compute the height and the base radius of the cylinder whose volume is the largest. Compute this largest volume.

The numbers $a=\frac{\sqrt[4]{8}}{2}$, $b=\frac{1}{2\sqrt[4]{8}}$, $c=\sqrt[4]{8}$, $d=\frac{2}{\sqrt[4]{8}}$ and $k=2^{-\frac{1}{4}}$ are given. The true equality is
(A) $k=a$
(B) $k=b$
(C) $k=c$
(D) $k=d$

The equation $\big||x|-2\big|=|x|+2$
(A) has no solutions.
(B) has exactly one solution.
(C) has exactly two solutions.
(D) has exactly four solutions.

The value of the expression $2\log_5 10-\frac{1}{\log_{20}5}$ is equal to
(A) $-1$
(B) $0$
(C) $1$
(D) $2$

The limit $\lim_{x\to 3^-}\frac{-x+2}{x^2-5x+6}$ is equal to
(A) $-\infty$
(B) $-1$
(C) $0$
(D) $+\infty$

The point $A=(-5,3)$ is the centre of symmetry of the graph of the linear fractional (homographic) function defined by the formula $f(x)=\frac{ax+7}{x+d}$ for $x\neq -d$. Compute the quotient $\frac{d}{a}$.
The tangent line to the parabola with equation $y=\sqrt{3}\,x^2-1$ at the point $P=(x_0,y_0)$ is inclined to the $Ox$ axis at an angle of $30^\circ$. Compute the coordinates of the point $P$.

The triangle $ABC$ is acute and $|AC|>|BC|$. The bisector $d_C$ of the angle $ACB$ intersects the side $AB$ at the point $K$. The point $L$ is the image of the point $K$ under the reflection in the bisector $d_A$ of the angle $BAC$, the point $M$ is the image of the point $L$ under the reflection in the bisector $d_C$ of the angle $ACB$, and the point $N$ is the image of the point $M$ under the reflection in the bisector $d_B$ of the angle $ABC$ (see the figure).
Prove that a circle can be circumscribed about the quadrilateral $KNML$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2018_p7_fig.png
Prove that for every integer $k$ and every integer $m$ the number $k^3m-km^3$ is divisible by $6$.

From the numbers of the eight-element set $Z=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9\}$ we form an eight-term sequence whose terms do not repeat. Compute the probability of the event that no two even numbers are adjacent terms of the sequence formed. Give the result as an irreducible common fraction.

The volume of a frustum of a cone (shown in the figure) can be computed from the formula $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi H\left(r^2+rR+R^2\right)$, where $r$ and $R$ are the radii of the bases ($r<R$), and $H$ is the height of the solid. A frustum of a cone is given whose height is equal to $10$, whose volume is $840\pi$, and $r=6$. Compute the cosine of the angle of inclination of a diagonal of the axial cross-section of this solid to one of its bases.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2018_p10_fig.png
Solve the equation $\sin 6x+\cos 3x=2\sin 3x+1$ in the interval $[0,\pi]$.
Find all values of the parameter $m$ for which the equation $x^2+(m+1)x-m^2+1=0$ has two real solutions $x_1$ and $x_2$ ($x_1\neq x_2$) satisfying the condition $x_1^3+x_2^3>-7x_1x_2$.

The terms of a geometric sequence $(a_n)$, defined for $n\ge 1$, satisfy the system of equations
$$\begin{cases} a_3+a_6=-84\\ a_4+a_7=168\end{cases}$$
Find the number $n$ of initial terms of this sequence whose sum $S_n$ is equal to $32769$.

The point $A=(7,-1)$ is a vertex of the isosceles triangle $ABC$ in which $|AC|=|BC|$. Both coordinates of the vertex $C$ are negative numbers. The circle inscribed in the triangle $ABC$ has the equation $x^2+y^2=10$. Compute the coordinates of the vertices $B$ and $C$ of this triangle.

We consider all isosceles trapezoids in which a circle can be inscribed and which satisfy the condition: the sum of the length of the longer base $a$ and the height of the trapezoid is equal to $2$.
a) Find all values of $a$ for which a trapezoid with the given properties exists.
b) Prove that the perimeter $L$ of such a trapezoid, as a function of the length $a$ of the longer base of the trapezoid, is given by the formula $L(a)=\frac{4a^2-8a+8}{a}$.
c) Compute the tangent of the acute angle of that one among the considered trapezoids whose perimeter is the smallest.

For any numbers $x>0$, $x\neq 1$, $y>0$, $y\neq 1$ the value of the expression $\left(\log_{\frac{1}{x}}y\right)\cdot\left(\log_{\frac{1}{y}}x\right)$ is equal to
(A) $x\cdot y$
(B) $\frac{1}{x\cdot y}$
(C) $-1$
(D) $1$

The number $\cos^2 105^\circ-\sin^2 105^\circ$ is equal to
(A) $-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
(B) $-\frac{1}{2}$
(C) $\frac{1}{2}$
(D) $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

The figure shows part of the graph of the function $y=f(x)$, which consists of two rays $AD$ and $CE$ and two segments $AB$ and $BC$, where $A=(-1,0)$, $B=(1,2)$, $C=(3,0)$, $D=(-4,3)$, $E=(6,3)$.
The formula of the function $f$ is
(A) $f(x)=|x+1|+|x-1|$
(B) $f(x)=\big||x-1|-2\big|$
(C) $f(x)=\big||x-1|+2\big|$
(D) $f(x)=|x-1|+2$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2019_p3_fig.png

The random events $A$ and $B$ contained in $\Omega$ are such that the probability $P(B')$ of the event $B'$, complementary to the event $B$, is equal to $\frac{1}{4}$. Moreover, the conditional probability $P(A\mid B)=\frac{1}{5}$. It follows that
(A) $P(A\cap B)=\frac{1}{20}$
(B) $P(A\cap B)=\frac{4}{15}$
(C) $P(A\cap B)=\frac{3}{20}$
(D) $P(A\cap B)=\frac{4}{5}$
Compute the limit $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{9n^3+11n^2}{7n^3+5n^2+3n+1}-\frac{n^2}{3n^2+1}\right).$$
We consider all five-digit natural numbers written using the digits $1$, $3$, $5$, $7$, $9$, without repeating any digit. Compute the sum of all such numbers.
The point $P=(10,2429)$ lies on the parabola with equation $y=2x^2+x+2219$. The line with slope-intercept equation $y=ax+b$ is tangent to this parabola at the point $P$. Compute the coefficient $b$.
Prove that for any positive real numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x<y$, and any positive real number $a$, the inequality $\frac{x+a}{y+a}+\frac{y}{x}>2$ holds.

An isosceles triangle $ABC$ is given in which $|AC|=|BC|$. A point $M$ ($M\neq A$ and $M\neq C$) is chosen on the leg $AC$ of this triangle, and a point $N$ is chosen on the leg $BC$ in such a way that $|AM|=|CN|$. Through the points $M$ and $N$ lines perpendicular to the base $AB$ of this triangle are drawn; they determine on it the points $S$ and $T$. Prove that $|ST|=\frac{1}{2}|AB|$.
The point $D$ lies on the side $AB$ of the triangle $ABC$, and $|AC|=16$, $|AD|=6$, $|CD|=14$ and $|BC|=|BD|$. Compute the perimeter of the triangle $ABC$.

The circles with equations $x^2+y^2-12x-8y+43=0$ and $x^2+y^2-2ax+4y+a^2-77=0$ are given. Find all values of the parameter $a$ for which these circles have exactly one common point. Consider all cases.

The three-term sequence $(a,b,c)$ with positive terms is arithmetic, while the sequence $\left(\frac{1}{a},\ \frac{2}{3b},\ \frac{1}{2a+2b+c}\right)$ is geometric. Compute the common ratio of the geometric sequence.

The polynomial defined by the formula $W(x)=2x^3+\left(m^3+2\right)x^2-11x-2(2m+1)$ is divisible by the binomial $(x-2)$, and when divided by the binomial $(x+1)$ it gives the remainder $6$. Compute $m$ and, for the value of $m$ found, solve the inequality $W(x)\le 0$.
Solve the equation $$(\cos x)\left[\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{2}\sin x.$$
Consider all regular triangular prisms with volume $V=2$. Find the edge lengths of that one among the considered prisms whose total surface area is the smallest. Compute this smallest area.

The polynomial $W$ defined by the formula $W(x)=x^{2019}-3x^{2000}+2x+6$
(A) is divisible by $(x-1)$ and gives remainder $6$ when divided by $(x+1)$.
(B) is divisible by $(x+1)$ and gives remainder $6$ when divided by $(x-1)$.
(C) is divisible by $(x-1)$ and is divisible by $(x+1)$.
(D) is divisible neither by $(x-1)$ nor by $(x+1)$.

The sequence $(a_n)$ is defined by the formula $a_n=\frac{3n^2+7n-5}{11-5n+5n^2}$ for every natural number $n\ge 1$. The limit of this sequence is equal to
(A) $3$
(B) $\frac{1}{5}$
(C) $\frac{3}{5}$
(D) $-\frac{5}{11}$

We have two urns. The first contains 3 white balls and 7 black balls, the second contains one white ball and 9 black balls. We roll a fair six-sided die, each face of which has a different number of pips, from one pip to six pips. If the roll shows the face with one pip, we draw one ball from the first urn; otherwise we draw one ball from the second urn. Then the probability of drawing a white ball is equal to
(A) $\frac{2}{15}$
(B) $\frac{1}{5}$
(C) $\frac{4}{5}$
(D) $\frac{13}{15}$

After transforming the algebraic expression $\left(x\sqrt{2}+y\sqrt{3}\right)^4$ into the form $ax^4+bx^3y+cx^2y^2+dxy^3+ey^4$, the coefficient $c$ is equal to
(A) $6$
(B) $36$
(C) $8\sqrt{6}$
(D) $12\sqrt{6}$

In the triangle $ABC$ the side $AB$ is $3$ times longer than the side $AC$, and the length of the side $BC$ is $\frac{4}{5}$ of the length of the side $AB$. Compute the cosine of the smallest angle of the triangle $ABC$.
Find all values of the parameter $a$ for which the equation $|x-5|=(a-1)^2-4$ has two distinct positive solutions.

An isosceles triangle $ABC$ is given in which $|AC|=|BC|=6$, and the point $D$ is the midpoint of the base $AB$. The circle with centre $D$ is tangent to the line $AC$ at the point $M$. The point $K$ lies on the side $AC$, the point $L$ lies on the side $BC$, the segment $KL$ is tangent to the circle under consideration, and $|KC|=|LC|=2$ (see the figure).
Prove that $\frac{|AM|}{|MC|}=\frac{4}{5}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/matura_2020_p7_fig.png
Positive numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfy the equality $a^2+2a=4b^2+4b$. Prove that $a=2b$.
Solve the equation $3\cos 2x+10\cos^2 x=24\sin x-3$ for $x\in[0,2\pi]$.

In a three-term geometric sequence $(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ the equality $a_1+a_2+a_3=\frac{21}{4}$ holds. The terms $a_1$, $a_2$, $a_3$ are, respectively, the fourth, the second and the first term of an increasing arithmetic sequence. Compute $a_1$.

The quadratic equation $x^2-(3m+2)x+2m^2+7m-15=0$ with unknown $x$ is given. Find all values of the parameter $m$ for which distinct solutions $x_1$ and $x_2$ of this equation exist and satisfy the condition $$2x_1^2+5x_1x_2+2x_2^2=2.$$

The line with equation $x+y-10=0$ intersects the circle with equation $x^2+y^2-8x-6y+8=0$ at the points $K$ and $L$. The point $S$ is the midpoint of the chord $KL$. Find the equation of the image of this circle under the homothety with centre $S$ and ratio $k=-3$.
Compute how many seven-digit natural numbers there are in whose decimal representation exactly three digits $1$ and exactly two digits $2$ occur.

The base of the quadrilateral pyramid $ABCDS$ is the trapezoid $ABCD$ ($AB\parallel CD$). The legs of this trapezoid have lengths $|AD|=10$ and $|BC|=16$, and the angle $ABC$ measures $30^\circ$. Each lateral face of this pyramid makes with the plane of the base an angle $\alpha$ such that $\tan\alpha=\frac{9}{2}$. Compute the volume of this pyramid.

The dimensions of the rectangular screen of a smartphone are to be designed so that the distances of the screen from the shorter edges of the smartphone are $0.5$ cm each, and the distances of the screen from the longer edges of the smartphone are $0.3$ cm each (the region between the screen and the edges of the smartphone is the frame). The screen itself is to have area $60\ \text{cm}^2$. Find those dimensions of the smartphone screen for which the area of the screen together with the frame is the smallest.

The difference $\cos^2 165^\circ-\sin^2 165^\circ$ is equal to
(A) $-1$
(B) $-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
(C) $-\frac{1}{2}$
(D) $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

The figure shows part of the graph of a function $f$ defined for every real number $x$.
One of the formulas given below is the formula of this function. Indicate the formula of the function $f$.
(A) $f(x)=\frac{\cos x+1}{|\cos x|+1}$
(B) $f(x)=\frac{\sin x+1}{|\sin x|+1}$
